title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed last week's benchmark improvements, discussed remaining VPC routing issues (NAT vs egress), TLS cert rotation plan, and a proposed maintenance window for runtime upgrade. Agreed on next steps: run focused latency tests, provide SOC2 docs, and schedule a brief maintenance window next Tuesday.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and network diagram by 2025-07-31
Customer to run targeted p95 latency test with 8k token prompts and share logs by 2025-08-01
Schedule maintenance window for runtime upgrade on 2025-08-05 (tentative)
Redwood SE to provide routing playbook and sample VPC route table changes
action_items: Michael Chen - send SOC2 + security pack - due 2025-07-31
Sara Patel - produce routing playbook and sample terraform snippets - due 2025-07-31
Jamal Ortiz - run p95 latency test and upload logs to shared folder - due 2025-08-01
Tomasz Nowak - confirm KMS integration details and access controls - due 2025-08-01
transcript:
Meeting header - 2025-07-30 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Sara Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Gomez (RDW Solutions), Jamal Ortiz (Atlas Platform), Priya Rao (Atlas SRE), Tomasz Nowak (Atlas Security), Ella Morgan (Atlas Product)

0:00 - Michael Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, hope the time still works. quick agenda - status on the network routing abnormalities, review last week's benchmark numbers, plan the upgrade, and call out any security blockers.
0:12 - Jamal Ortiz: yep this is fine. we saw some intermittent egress failures when we tested cross-account peering last thursday, small window but it affected p95.
0:20 - Sara Patel: thanks Jamal. we dug into the logs and it looks like a route table overwrite from a terraform apply caused the NAT gateway attachment to get deprioritized - so some outbound packets tried to route via the transit gateway incorrectly.
0:30 - Priya Rao: yeah we have the apply in our audit logs - there was a module change rolled last week. the weird thing is it only showed up under heavier load, so maybe the kernel queues or iptables conntrack state were getting exhausted?
0:46 - Luis Gomez: oh interesting, could be conntrack timeouts. we also observed a spike in new connections during the benchmark run that correlates with the p95 spikes.
0:55 - Michael Chen: ok that aligns. for context - our runtime upgrade we want to do includes a kernel-level optimization and updated batching kernel which should reduce per-token latency, but it requires a brief restart of the inference service instance.
1:10 - Ella Morgan: how long is brief? we need to let product know for downstream SLAs.
1:14 - Sara Patel: expecting a rolling restart per node, roughly 3-7 minutes per instance in the cluster, total window depends on parallelism. with canary first, we typically keep availability targets and have automated fallback to hosted endpoints if you need absolute zero downtime.
1:30 - Jamal Ortiz: for this pilot we want to avoid hitting our external failover, ideally keep everything internal. is there a recommended maintenance window?
1:38 - Michael Chen: Tue morning 06:00 UTC tends to be low traffic for most orgs; we can do that week of Aug 4th. we'll provide exact start times and a runbook.
1:47 - Tomasz Nowak: on the security side, we need more detail on key rotation and KMS access. earlier you mentioned optional HSM integration for on-prem. can you confirm what secrets we need to expose?
2:05 - Sara Patel: yes - for VPC/private deployment the only thing Redwood needs is an IAM role for the control-plane agent to pull model bundles and to access S3 encryption keys, all model payloads remain in your VPC. for KMS we support customer-managed keys, and we can also integrate with on-prem HSM over PKCS#11 in the private package. we'll send the exact permissions list.
2:22 - Tomasz Nowak: ok please send the IAM policy, and a diagram of where the control-plane sits relative to the model servers. we need to validate with our audit team.
2:30 - Michael Chen: noted - action item. we'll include the network diagram and the control-plane flow.
2:36 - Priya Rao: back to the numbers - can we quickly recap the benchmark results you shared last week? we saw CPU and GPU utilization differences across models and quantization profiles.
2:48 - Luis Gomez: quick recap - with quantization profile q4-0 we saw ~18% cost reduction and p50 latency improved about 10% versus fp16 baseline. p95 improvements were less consistent due to warmup variance. tokens per second increased from 120 to ~145 on our test instance (A100-like).
3:05 - Jamal Ortiz: good. but the p95 variability is what worried us - could be due to KV cache coldstarts or the routing issue.
3:12 - Sara Patel: exactly - two hypotheses: routing-induced retries and cache cold miss patterns when requests land on different nodes. we recommended enabling sticky routing to reduce cache misses during the trial which would improve p95.
3:25 - Ella Morgan: sticky routing - does that affect load balancing or burst handling?
3:30 - Sara Patel: small tradeoff - sticky routing pins sessions to a node which improves cache locality but can reduce ability to spread sudden bursts; we can configure session TTLs and a fallback to round-robin when CPU exceeds threshold.
3:45 - Priya Rao: what's the TTL you'd suggest?
3:48 - Sara Patel: for your workload we suggest 30 minutes session affinity, with adaptive fallback at 75% CPU. we'll add these snippets to the routing playbook.
3:58 - Michael Chen: also want to call out the TLS cert rotation - we pushed a cert rotation test yesterday and observed one node that didn't pick up the new cert due to an old cert path in the startup script. that was fixed.
4:12 - Jamal Ortiz: yep we saw that in the logs, it resulted in a short TLS negotiation failure for one client and a reconnection. it's resolved now but we want a robust rotation plan.
4:22 - Sara Patel: we'll provide a rotation runbook, and we can optionally do certs via your internal PKI or let Redwood manage certs inside the VPC - depends on your compliance preferences.
4:35 - Tomasz Nowak: we prefer to manage certs and keys internally, and Redwood to show how the agent will pick up rotated certs automatically.
4:44 - Michael Chen: understood. action item to document cert rotation behaviour and KMS flows.
4:50 - Luis Gomez: quick note on metrics - we added a new dashboard tile that shows token-level cost and latency breakdown per route, that should help you spot regressions quickly.
4:58 - Ella Morgan: can you share a link?
5:00 - Michael Chen: yes I'll send the console link after the call - noted.
5:08 - Jamal Ortiz: about the routing fix - we'll revert the terraform module change for the route table and schedule a controlled apply in your staging first. after that we will re-run the p95 tests.
5:20 - Priya Rao: we will also enable conntrack tuning on the nodes as a precaution.
5:28 - Sara Patel: great, once you revert we recommend running a 30-minute steady-state load with synthetic traffic and then a spike test. that should isolate warm cache behavior.
5:40 - Michael Chen: timeline check - jamal will run the tests and upload logs by Aug 1, we (Redwood) provide SOC2 and network diagrams by Jul 31, and we'll tentatively schedule the upgrade for Aug 5 with a canary.
5:56 - Jamal Ortiz: sounds good. one question on rollback - if the new runtime shows a regression in p95, what's the rollback path?
6:04 - Sara Patel: rollback is straightforward - we keep the previous runtime as a pinned image and can flip traffic back in under five minutes. we also can route affected traffic to hosted endpoints as a temporary measure.
6:15 - Tomasz Nowak: ensure rollback instructions are in the runbook and that we have an audit trail for who initiated it.
6:20 - Michael Chen: absolutely. we'll include audit steps and an approval gate.
6:25 - Ella Morgan: any blockers from Redwood's side for the maintenance window?
6:29 - Michael Chen: none on our end; Sara will lead implementation and Luis will monitor metrics.
6:35 - Closing - quick recap of action items and owners, agree to reconvene same time next week, unless we need an emergency sync after tests.
6:45 - Michael Chen: thanks everyone. we'll send the docs and links.

End of transcript

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and shorthand; speaker labels were normalized for clarity.
